title: Bytes read by a tiled GEMM
starter:
let tile_bytes (n : int) (bm : int) : int =
  let blocks = n / bm in
  let floats_per_block = bm * n in
  blocks * floats_per_block * 4
hints: A tile of C has rows and columns. If `n / bm` tiles fit across, how many fit in the whole of C?
A block reads its rows of A and also its columns of B. The starter counts only one of the two.
The blocks are `(n / bm) * (n / bm)`, and one block reads `2 * bm * n` floats. The last line is already right.
explain: C is cut into `n / bm` tiles each way, so there are `(n / bm) * (n / bm)` blocks. One block reads `bm` rows of A and `bm` columns of B, each `n` long, which is `2 * bm * n` floats of 4 bytes. For 768 with 16 by 16 tiles that is 2,304 blocks times 24,576 floats times 4, about 226 MB. With 64 by 64 tiles it is about 57 MB, a quarter as much.
